edge_explainer: No single crash - only ONE >7% day in four months (+13.1% on the 05-12 Q1 print). The -43.8% is multiple compression from a euphoric 2025-09-11 high of 199.24 after two consecutive EPS misses (Q4'25 03-03, Q1'26 05-12) against a revenue line that never slowed. Gate fired on FY27 rev growth 21.4% / Q1'26 yoy 46.6% = 0.46, but FY26e revenue growth is +30.6% and estimates are rising (FY26e EPS +1.3%, FY27e +4.9% over 90d) - a false fire; the one amber is that the last 30 days of revisions skew 3-down/1-up. The deceleration the annual figures hide is SEQUENTIAL: Q1'26 added only +3.6% q/q after three quarters of +8.6/+13.8/+14.5%. Ruling DE-RATE: revenue compounding 30%+, operating income -1,133 -> 343 -> 662 -> 1,985 $M across FY22-FY25, forward estimates flat-to-up. Cap structure pulled first: 612.48M shares all-classes (not 566.96M in the feed), $3.58B debt vs $10.54B cash+STI = $6.96B net cash, EV $61.6B = 2.06x FY26e EV/S, 21.3x FY27e P/E. CAVEAT on that net cash: Sea funds with convertibles historically and the debt line does not disclose the convert/strike split - the 20-F equity note was not read, so 'net cash' is provisional. TOP UNVERIFIABLE and the real risk: Monee is a consumer lender operating inside its own marketplace with 20M borrowers; provisioning is the honesty channel there (an originator that also books the loan can defer credit recognition by extending duration and it looks like operating leverage until it does not). No NPL, provision or vintage data could be pulled from primary sources this pass. That is a gap, not a clean.
